annotation.title_clean: The Interpretation and Application of International Humanitarian Law in Relation to Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems
annotation.title_en: The Interpretation and Application of International Humanitarian Law in Relation to Lethal Autonomous Weapon Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: UNIDIR (United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research)
annotation.summary_en: UNIDIR publication page for a 36-page background paper summarising publicly available State, scholarly and expert views on how international humanitarian law applies to lethal autonomous weapon systems. It finds shared agreement that IHL applies but persistent divergences and underexamined rules.
key_provisions_or_claims: All contributors agree IHL applies to development and use of LAWS.
Views diverge in form and content, making comparison difficult.
Some IHL rules governing LAWS remain underexamined.
Proposed civilian-protection measures often don't specify their IHL basis.
Measures before and after attacks are needed for compliance and accountability.
